results_numeric.quantity: Disk-averaged excitation temperature DCO+ vs DCN

evidence.quote: DCO$^+$ appears colder than DCN (33 vs 66 K)
Between 25–70 au, the best-fit DCO$^+$ excitation temperatures are 37–39.5 K

findings_qualitative.value: DCN and DCO+ both show inner cavities; DCN is a narrow ring near 30 au with a halo, DCO+ a broad structured ring extending beyond the pebble disk

evidence.quote: most DCN emission originates from a narrow ring peaking around 30 au

claims.hypothesis: DCO+ emits from cold midplane near the CO snow surface
claims.experiment: Multi-line rotational diagrams in radial bins
claims.finding: DCO+ originates in an elevated, warmer layer

evidence.quote: DCO$^+$ originates in a layer that is more elevated than the CO snow surface

claims.result: 66 K vs 33 K, DCN poorly constrained

evidence.quote: we cannot exclude that the actual DCN excitation temperature is $<$40 K

claims.hypothesis: Simple abundance/temperature-boundary models explain the emission
claims.result: DCN fit by 25 au hole and constant abundance where T>20 K; DCO+ needs increasing abundance or a second cold reservoir

evidence.quote: DCO$^+$ cannot be fit by any single constant abundance distribution

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Continuum opacity alone as the cause of central cavities, rejected since optically thin 13C18O is centrally peaked

evidence.loc: 3.1 DCN and DCO$^+$ emission maps and spectra
evidence.quote: Continuum opacity cannot be the whole explanation for these central cavities, however
